risks: Small rooms make the gap thin. If the player rests at the rubble station, a second fall in the lane costs only seconds more than a first fall. The weight then comes from the death sequence, the reverted find and the refreshed-pull logic, not from time. Nothing here is validated: it must be played before any claim that it 'feels weighty'.

Skipping the optional rubble rest means a second lane fall replays the solved door puzzle (about 25-30 s, the 30 s cap). That brushes against AbleGamers' 'don't repeat solved challenges' guidance. It is a deliberate player choice, but it needs a clear station light and prompt.

Honesty now affects survival odds (two falls plus one pull, against two falls). This needs Nathanial's explicit confirmation under the rule that choices carry no automatic penalty. Keep the gap to one knockdown and never touch the controls.
Hidden tiers confuse players. The shaken mark and death-card line must state, in text plus shape, what the next fall does.
Exploit: quitting during a death to dodge a fall. The fall must resolve before the quit record is written. Pause's current cancel-without-restoring path must change.

Large test churn. impact_test, junction_test and sentry_test assert the autosave A-D restores and compare save bytes, so they must be rewritten. Removing the Records autosaves changes chapter_scene_test expectations.

The rubble station at about x 496 is tight against CHOICE_X 526, WOLF_RUBBLE_X 448 and his 62 px body. Overlapping sprites and reach could fire the lane question or the station by mistake. Verify with rendered stills.
WOLF's pull needs authored animation and pathing into the blast, lane and cloud, with Reduced Motion variants, while keeping the ±4 px event positions.
A crash (not a quit) in Records before the exit rest loses up to about 90 s, and the mirror choice can be remade.
Death-sequence comfort. The ringing tone and screen drain need a modest level and a short length, because there is no toggle. Reduced Motion must cover the collapse and drain motion.
Migrating v4 saves through a one-shot quit record is unusual. If the record fails validation, the player falls back to New Game unless the v4 file is kept until the first v5 rest.
Scope mismatch: the relayed user request ('update the hero and game main screen background screen everywhere as well with codex') is not addressed by this design step and still needs its own task.
test_plan: m0_state_test: v5 round-trip for each safe_point_id. Reject an unknown id. Reject junction_rubble without door_blown and records_exit without chapter_complete. collected and secured arrays are written sorted and compared byte for byte.

m0_state_test: quit-record validation. Falls outside 0-1 are rejected. pull_used with press_without_warning is rejected. Unsecured entries not in collected are rejected. A state before the checkpoint is accepted only in the quit record, and _read_checkpoint still rejects it as a lasting save.

m0_state_test: v4 migration. A v4 file from each old autosave (Records purge, A, B, C, D) loads as a one-shot quit record with memory, route and flags intact. The v4 file is not deleted until the first v5 rest.

death_test (new): the first lethal hit in each segment (blast, sentry, cloud) with press_without_warning sets falls to 1, restores the beat snapshot nearby (valve-rebuild or rubble-line), keeps memory bytes, writes nothing to disk and keeps the save file's mtime and bytes unchanged.

death_test: the second lethal hit before resting loads the last rest from disk, sets falls to 0, clears shaken, refreshes the pull and puts unsecured finds back at their spawn spots. Skipping the rubble rest re-seals the door (door_blown false).
death_test: a vent hit never changes falls and never writes. Three vent knockdowns in a row leave falls at 0.

wolf_pull_test: disclose_risk with WOLF within 200 px and the pull unused turns the first lethal hit into a knockdown with falls still 0. A survived blast commits door_blown. A second lethal hit then counts as the first fall. With wolf_baiting true, or WOLF more than 200 px away, there is no pull. press_without_warning never pulls. Resting refreshes the pull.

safe_point_test: a held USE at each station writes exactly one file with the right safe_point_id and moves unsecured to secured. A failed write (read-only path) keeps you at the station with the error hint and falls unchanged. The rubble station is unreachable before the blast (engineer x capped at 438). The station's reach never overlaps CHOICE_X or the breaker and valve reach spans.
save_writer_audit test: drive the full route (corridor, Records, junction) and count disk writes. Only the 4 rests write. The purge, mirror and junction A, B and C points no longer write.

quit_test: Return to Title mid-beat writes the quit record at the beat start, not the exact position. Continue loads it with falls and pull_used carried, then deletes it. A second Continue loads the last rest. Quitting during a death resolves the fall first: the quit record shows falls 1, or the rest state after a second fall. New Game deletes both files.

presentation_test: the death sequence disables controls, ducks the bus to the tone and shows the card. Input is ignored before 2.4 s on the first death of a beat and before 0.8 s on a repeat of the same beat. The card never auto-advances. Reduced Motion skips the tilt, slide and drain motion but keeps the fade and card. WOLF's reaction branch matches memory.choice_id.

engineer_only_route_test: with press_without_warning and no WOLF help, the whole route can be completed with a scripted death at every threat, and progress never gets stuck after any sequence of first falls, second falls and quits.

Report separately: headless logic (the tests above), rendered stills (rubble station placement, shaken HUD, case markers, death card), and hands-on play of the junction route. Make no game-feel claim until that play is done.

drafts.name: Secure Copy: facts persist, the body and the unsecured case go back to the last safe point
drafts.pitch: This is a design proposal only. I edited, ran and played nothing, and every timing below is worked out from code constants. Death and progress get two separate ledgers. (1) FACTS: anything the engineer has done in the world (the relay memory, the opened seal, the Records traces, the blown door, the downed sentry, a cleared junction, every pickup). Facts are written the moment they happen by the existing silent autosaves. A death never undoes a fact, so a solved puzzle or a seen conversation is never replayed. This follows Dark Souls shortcuts and the AbleGamers advice not to repeat completed challenges. (2) THE BODY AND THE CASE: where the engineer stands and which evidence is made safe. Only a physical SAFE POINT, used with a short held-USE ritual, moves the respawn point and secures the case. A death sends the engineer back to the last safe point they used, which may be in the previous room. Evidence picked up since that safe point is UNSECURED. On death it drops where the engineer fell and can be recovered once. Dying again before recovering it loses it for good, as with Hollow Knight's Shade, Shovel Knight's money bags and Darkwood's dropped inventory. Weight therefore comes from three things, and only a little from replay time (Juul: time is the currency, but loss and change also count): the grim death sequence Nathanial decided on, a real but bounded stake in the case, and WOLF remembering that he saw the engineer die. Safe points matter because they are the only places that (a) move your respawn, (b) make the case safe and (c) let you rest: quiet, no threats and a WOLF moment, like Resident Evil safe rooms, Signalis save rooms and The Bunker's lanterns. Small slice rooms keep the longest forced walk to about 8 s, and the only content that repeats is the hazard that killed you. Steam from the vent still only knocks the engineer down and retries the beat, so the hazard's size tells you how serious the failure is. Sekiro and Elden Ring use the same two-tier shape, but here it is keyed to the hazard, not to a hidden counter. There is no accessibility toggle and no counter on screen.
drafts.on_death:
KILLERS, all in the Service Junction:
- The door blast: standing in 360-540 when the fuse ends.
- Sentry contact during a chase (40 px).
- Staying in the coolant cloud. Entering it starts a cough stagger with a frost edge and a COOLANT label. Controls stay normal. Remaining inside for 1.2 s in a row kills. The cloud is 634-766 and the engineer moves at 190 px/s, so crossing it takes about 0.7 s.

The vent steam (264-336 plus half a body) stays a KNOCKDOWN. It keeps today's _fail_beat path: it restores the in-memory beat_snapshot, costs nothing from the case and never moves the respawn.

DEATH SEQUENCE (new _die(cause), separate from _fail_beat; about 5 s before the card, then player-paced):
1. Collapse. The engineer folds down. There is no gore, no blood decal and no dismemberment. Reduced Motion uses a cut to the fallen pose.
2. Sound. Every bus ducks to a single procedural ringing tone at a capped volume for about 1.5 s. The tone also gets an on-screen caption.
3. The screen drains to desaturated, then dark, over about 1.5 s.
4. WOLF reacts by his own choice, keyed to memory.choice_id:
   - DISCLOSE (honest at the relay): he rushes to the engineer, lowers his head and nudges them.
   - PRESS_WITHOUT_WARNING: he stops at a distance, holds and looks away. He does not leave.
5. A short death card names the cause in one line. It holds for at least 1.2 s, then waits for USE, because text is player-paced. Pause still works.
6. Respawn at the last safe point used, with a fade in. At that moment the save is already written: unsecured items have moved to `dropped` at the death x, a previous `dropped` set has moved to `lost` (the tool excepted), and falls_witnessed has gone up. Writing it before the card means quitting during the card cannot undo the death.

WHAT THE WORLD DOES AFTER A DEATH:
- Facts stand. If the engineer died in the blast, the door still blew. This fact is committed at the existing autosave B and is the realistic outcome.
- Live hazards re-sync from facts as _sync_junction_room does today: sentry patrolling from 840 or down at 700, arm rewound, cloud cleared.
- lane_choice is kept for the session, so WOLF does not re-ask "How do we bring it down?" (Research 3 flagged that re-asking reads oddly).
- Re-entering a room you have already solved plays a one-line condensed status. It never replays the authored entry, WOLF scouting or a choice.
drafts.what_safe_points_do:
A SAFE POINT is a lit wall station. It is the ONLY thing that:
1. MOVES THE RESPAWN. Death returns you to the last safe point you used, and nothing else changes that. Autosaves A-D and the Records saves still write facts to disk, but they no longer decide where you wake. This is the purpose Nathanial said was missing: today the junction autosaves are the respawn points, so the corridor station only matters as a place to quit.
2. SECURES THE CASE. Every UNSECURED entry becomes SECURED and can never drop again. Fiction: the station backs the copies up beyond the Director's reach, which fits the purge theme.
3. IS A RITUAL. Hold USE for about 1.0 s, reusing hold_use. It plays a distinct station tone, and the room tone drops while you stand there. The design follows the RE typewriter, the Alien keycard and the Signalis TV. Every station sits where no hazard or sentry can reach, so it is a true rest like an RE safe room or a Signalis save room. It is not an Alien-style save that can be interrupted, because the slice's threats are telegraphed puzzles, not a hunter.
4. IS A WOLF MOMENT. If WOLF is within reach he chooses to settle and sit, as his resting cue. The first use of each station carries one authored exchange. The corridor keeps its existing checkpoint_callback, which teaches the station's job as SH2 (2024) does with its first save point.
5. WRITES THE SAVE with a positions snapshot at the station. If the write fails, the existing save_pending and "press USE again" behaviour applies.

Stations never heal, never refill and never count anything. They do not respawn threats either: Dark Souls bonfires do, but here that would force repeats.
drafts.what_is_lost_and_kept:
KEPT through any death, quit or Continue (FACTS, written when they happen):
- The relay memory (choice_id and the exact words seen), route and mirror_route.
- The purge and mirror traces, and the derived REC entries in the case, which are never at risk.
- door_open, chapter_complete, door_blown, sentry_down, junction_cleared.
- SECURED case entries.
- The carried tool: it is never permanently lost (see below).
- falls_witnessed.
- Settings.

LOST on death:
- Position. Engineer and WOLF go back to the last safe point, possibly one or two rooms back.
- Live hazard progress: the pressure build, valve turns, arm wind-up and sentry position. These re-sync from facts.
- UNSECURED case entries. They drop together as one 'dropped case' prop at the death x, clamped to walkable floor and to x+14 ≤ 452 while the door is unblown. One USE (a tap) recovers them all as UNSECURED again. If you die again before recovering them, they become LOST, as with Hollow Knight's Shade and Shovel Knight's bags: shown in the case as LOST, with their room, never hidden and never faked.
- Exception: an unsecured TOOL is never LOST. On a second death it returns to its original pickup spot, so an optional method cannot be removed for good.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY AT RISK IN THIS SLICE (bounded on purpose):
- The corridor and Records have no hazards.
- [OBJECT_JUNCTION] at the junction entry is at risk until the junction station.
- [DATA_RECORDS] is at risk if you skip the Records station.
- [LOG_LANE] only appears once sentry_down is true, so it can never be at risk.
- At most 2 optional entries can ever be at stake. Nothing required is ever lost.

KNOCKDOWN (vent): nothing is lost. It retries the beat from beat_snapshot as today.
drafts.wolf_role:
WOLF is a witness and keeps watch over rests. He never revives, rescues or carries anything.

AT DEATH: he chooses his reaction from memory. Under DISCLOSE he rushes in and nudges the engineer; under PRESS he holds back at a distance and looks away. This is Nathanial's decided reaction and is presentation only. The engineer-only route and the controls are identical under both choices.

AT RESPAWN: he is already at the safe point beside the engineer. His first respawn line differs by choice_id and falls_witnessed (0, 1, or 2+, capped). The tier picks an authored line variant, so his words carry the memory of seeing them die, which is the Amnesia 'something changes after each death' idea in character form. It is never shown as a number or meter and changes no mechanics. From the third death on he uses a short line or simply a look, so lines do not repeat into comedy (Grip on repetition).

AT SAFE POINTS: he settles and sits when he is in reach, and the first use of each station has an exchange.

AT THE DROPPED CASE: under DISCLOSE he may stand by it as a cue. Both routes get the same glowing prop marker, so this is never a mechanical advantage.

REJECTED FOR THIS SLICE: a WOLF rescue that turns one lethal hit per safe-point visit into a knockdown (the Far Cry 2 and Prince of Persia precedents). It would cut the weight Nathanial asked for and tie survival odds to honesty. Revisit it only if he wants honesty to affect survival, and only after a played build.
drafts.ties_to_evidence_case:
The case is what you risk and what the safe points protect. This makes the story theme (the Director purging records) the save system's stake, and it never blocks progress.
- STATUS WORDS. Each case entry carries one, shown as text plus a shape so meaning never depends on colour alone: SECURED, UNSECURED, DROPPED (with the room) or LOST (with the room).
- WHAT IS NEVER AT RISK. The derived purge and mirror records are facts.
- PICKUPS. A pickup now WRITES TO DISK as a fact with secured=false. The current inventory design only patches beat_snapshot, so this is a change to that design. Writing at pickup means a quit or crash never deletes a find, and Continue keeps it at risk.
- THE DROPPED CASE. It is one physical prop with its own handling sound. Recovering it uses the same tap and 'Stowed' toast as a normal pickup.
- NOTHING IS SPENT. No completion count, no percentage, and LOST entries are never needed for anything.
- THE TOOL. Same rule, but it can never become LOST, so an optional station method cannot vanish.
- SAVE FORMAT. This rides on the planned SAVE_VERSION 5 inventory bump, so there is one migration, not two.
placement_per_room: CORRIDOR (no hazards): the existing SAFE POINT at x 876, past the seal at 752-808. It becomes the held-USE ritual and is the tutorial station, keeping its existing checkpoint_callback line as WOLF's first exchange. The [TOOL_A] pickup (about x 470) and [LOG_CORRIDOR] come before it, so both are always secured before any danger. A second USE still enters Records, as today.

RECORDS ACCESS (no hazards): a NEW SAFE POINT at about x 690. That is the free floor between the mirror port's reach (462-578) and the exit's reach (772-888), and clear of [DATA_RECORDS] at 300-420. Its role is 'last rest before the junction', like an RE safe room before a fight, and WOLF settles there. Skipping it is the meaningful choice: [DATA_RECORDS] goes into the junction unsecured, and a junction death sends you back to the corridor. The existing Records autosaves stay as fact writes only. The exact x must pass a geometry test against the station reaches.

SERVICE JUNCTION (all killers): a NEW SAFE POINT in the blown-door niche at about x 500, with reach ±20. It is shown dark and unreachable behind the seal until door_blown (door rule x+14 ≤ 452), so it is earned by surviving the blast, which is the Dark Souls 'bonfire after the hard part' shape. It sits behind the rubble, outside the sentry's reach (CHASE_MIN_X ≈ 586), so it is a true rest. It must not overlap the inert valve reach (≤472), WOLF_RUBBLE_X 448 or the lane-choice point CHOICE_X ≈ 526. If a geometry test shows a clash, move it into 452-520 or, as a fallback, to the left wall at about x 140, which is weaker. There is no station between the lane and the hatch: after sentry_down nothing can kill you, and autosave D just writes the cleared fact.

REPEAT BUDGET (worked out from constants, not played): The worst case uses only the corridor station and dies in the blast. Corridor to Records is about 3.7 s of walk, to the junction about 2.5 s, plus 2 USE transitions, so about 8 s of walking through solved rooms. The failed blast then repeats (breaker, about a 6 s build, 3 turns, retreat), about 14 s. Total forced repeat is about 22-25 s, excluding the death sequence and card. Using the Records station cuts the walk to about 4 s. Using the junction station cuts a lane death to about 1 s of walk plus the sentry encounter you failed. For later chapters, keep stations spaced so there are at most 2-3 minutes of uncertain play between them, and never so a solved puzzle or dialogue must be replayed.
drafts.quitting_and_continue:
QUITTING (Pause, Return to Title, closing the window, or a mobile app kill) never costs a fact or a find. Every fact and pickup was already written when it happened, and a death is written before its card appears. Quitting does no extra write and so cannot be used to undo a death or keep a drop; this also prevents save-scumming.

CONTINUE loads the single save file and resumes at the LAST SAFE POINT USED, in that room, with all facts, every case status (UNSECURED stays unsecured, a DROPPED case stays where it fell) and falls_witnessed. A one-line status says where you are. The worst positional loss from quitting mid-junction is the walk back from the last station, about 4-8 s. Sirlin's rule ('no meaningful progress lost on stopping') and the Game Accessibility Guidelines' concern for players who play in short bursts are met without any toggle.

The title screen enables Continue as today: only when a valid save exists, and checkpoint_reached is still required, so nothing is saved before the corridor station and NO_CHECKPOINT_NOTE is unchanged. New Game clears everything as today.

MIGRATION: a v4 save in Records or in the junction with the door sealed loads at the new Records station. A v4 junction save with door_blown loads at the junction station. A v4 corridor save loads at the corridor station. Existing entries all count as SECURED. Migration is generous on purpose, so no existing save loses anything.
player_facing_text_needed: Death cards, one per cause (blast, sentry, coolant), plus the continue prompt. Placeholders: [DEATH_CARD_BLAST], [DEATH_CARD_SENTRY], [DEATH_CARD_COOLANT], [DEATH_CARD_PROMPT]. The wording is Nathanial's: grim, not gory, one line each.
The caption for the ringing tone, for players who cannot hear it (e.g. [CAPTION_RINGING]).
WOLF's death reaction under DISCLOSE and under PRESS. These are mostly action; any line or vocal is optional and needs approval.

WOLF's respawn lines: first death under DISCLOSE, first death under PRESS, a second-death variant for each, and a short line or a look-only beat from the third death on. Placeholders [WOLF_FALL_1_D], [WOLF_FALL_1_P], [WOLF_FALL_2_D], [WOLF_FALL_2_P].
The safe point station label and hold prompt (e.g. 'SAFE POINT' and 'Hold E: secure'), including the touch-button label.
Safe point confirmation (e.g. 'Case secured.'), with no counts or percentages.
WOLF's first-use exchanges at the Records station and the junction station. The corridor keeps its existing callback.
Case status words SECURED, UNSECURED, DROPPED and LOST, plus the 'Dropped in [room]' and 'Lost in [room]' detail lines.
The dropped-case prop prompt and recovery toast (e.g. 'E: recover case').
The message when entries become LOST, and the message when the tool returns to its pickup spot.
The COOLANT warning label and the cough-stagger cue text, if any.
The condensed re-entry status lines for Records and the junction after a respawn, replacing the authored entry, WOLF scouting and the lane question.
The Continue resume status (e.g. 'Resumed at the [room] safe point.').
Retired: today's 'Back at the last autosave.' becomes death-only. The vent knockdown keeps 'Back at the start of this beat.' Confirm both.

Public docs: a spoiler-light 'Safe points and death' first-play explanation, an updated save guide (Continue resumes at the last safe point; facts are never lost; unsecured finds can drop) and a changelog entry.
drafts.save_model:
One file, user://m0-save.json, still written atomically via .tmp and a rename. SAVE_VERSION goes to 5 and shares the inventory bump.

NEW FIELDS:
- safe_point: String, one of "corridor", "records" or "junction". The room is derived from this; positions are the station positions.
- case: {secured, unsecured, lost: sorted Array[String] of known ids; dropped: {} or {items: sorted Array[String], room: String, x: float}}.
- falls_witnessed: int 0..2, capped.

chapter_id now means the FURTHEST room reached. The resume room comes from safe_point. The v4 rule 'outside the junction the three junction flags must be false' therefore becomes 'junction flags require chapter_id == junction', whatever room you resume in.

V5 VALIDATION BLOCK, run after the v4 block:
- safe_point is a known id, and its room ≤ chapter_id in chapter order.
- safe_point "junction" requires door_blown.
- The lists are disjoint, contain only known ids, are sorted and have no duplicates.
- The tool id is never in lost.
- dropped.x is between 40 and 920, dropped.room ≤ chapter_id, and in the junction with the door unblown x+14 ≤ 452.
- Derived REC ids never appear in any list.

WRITERS:
- Fact writes: the existing autosaves, pickups and recovery.
- The station write, which is the only writer of safe_point and positions.
- The death write, which moves unsecured to dropped, the old dropped set to lost and increments falls_witnessed, before the card appears.

The knockdown path still restores beat_snapshot in memory and does not write. The existing save_pending retry on the next USE covers a failed write.

Lists are written sorted so the byte-comparing tests stay deterministic, and their expected bytes are regenerated in the same change.

Migration v4 → v5 (see Continue): every existing entry becomes secured, falls_witnessed=0, and safe_point is mapped generously.
references: Jesper Juul, 'Fear of Failing? The Many Meanings of Difficulty in Video Games' and 'In Search of Lost Time': punishment types, time as the currency of failure, and players preferring to feel responsible.
Jesper Juul, The Art of Failure (MIT Press, 2013): the paradox of failure.

Thomas Grip (Frictional), 'Alien: Isolation and The Two Hardest Problems in Horror' (2014) and 'The Problem of Repetition' (2011): death brings relief, repetition kills fear, change something after a death.
Amnesia: Rebirth / SOMA / Amnesia: The Bunker (Dread Central 2023): a post-death price, a later Safe Mode, and a return to scarce manual lantern saves in a safe room.
Alien: Isolation, Alistair Hope in Game Informer Afterwords (2014), plus Steam discussions: the save ritual as part of the horror, and the burnout from long replays.
Resident Evil typewriters and safe rooms (Kill Screen; Laced Records; Film Stories 2022), and the RE2 remake hybrid of autosave plus typewriter (Thumbsticks 2019; Twinfinite).
Signalis (rose-engine): threat-free red-TV save rooms and the 'comfort is wrong' philosophy (Dread Central; Vice; TechRadar).
Silent Hill 2 (2024): the first save point placed as a tutorial (Lenart, MP1st).
Dark Souls (Miyazaki, Game Informer 2009; New Yorker via NME): recoverable souls and bonfires as relief, and shortcuts that persist.
Hollow Knight (Hollow Knight wiki): the Shade holds Geo and a second death loses it.
Shovel Knight (Yacht Club, 'Checkpoint Design'): dropped gold bags recoverable once.
Darkwood: on death you drop half your inventory at a spot marked on the map.
Sekiro (Xbox Wire; TheGamer) and Elden Ring Stakes of Marika (Fextralife): two-tier death and respawn.
Limbo (Jensen, 'Hanging in Limbo'), Inside reviews and Celeste (Klepek, Vice 2018): short repeats keep weight without tedium.
Far Cry 2 buddy rescue and Prince of Persia (2008) Elika (Game Developer): considered and rejected for this slice.
Hellblade rot (Antoniades, PCGamesN): felt stakes without fake consequences, cited as a boundary not to cross.
David Sirlin (Game Developer 2008): stopping must not lose meaningful progress.
AbleGamers 'Save Early, Save Often' and Game Accessibility Guidelines (manual save, intermediate).
Cuerdo, Mahajan & Melcer, 'Die-r Consequences' (IEEE CoG 2021), abstract only: the respawn point shifts autonomy, mastery and immersion.
risks: The biggest code risk is cross-room respawn. It separates the resume room (safe_point) from chapter_id, relaxes the v4 rule that junction flags are false outside the junction, and needs enter_records and enter_junction to allow re-entry into an already solved room with condensed lines instead of authored ones. Records exit art hidden after chapter close and the wolf_scouting and relay_refused transients must re-sync correctly.

Permanent LOST evidence may feel punitive for optional story content. Nathanial must confirm permanence. The fallback is that a twice-dropped entry returns to its original spot (logs back to their screen), which keeps the walk-back stake but removes permanence.

Keeping the door blown after a blast death means you can 'solve' the blast by dying. It costs the death sequence, the walk back and the case drop, which is honest, but Nathanial may prefer that a blast death re-seals the door, which repeats the about 14 s puzzle instead.
Juul shows blame shifts to the game if a kill is not clearly telegraphed. The new 1.2 s coolant choke window and the lane need hands-on play before any claim about fairness or feel.
Repetition kills fear (Grip). Repeated lane deaths will wear out the sentry and WOLF's lines, so cap the line variants and fall back to a look-only reaction.
The ringing tone must be volume-capped, short and captioned. The collapse and drain need Reduced Motion and photosensitivity-safe variants. There is no toggle, so the defaults must be safe.
falls_witnessed must never surface as a number or meter, and must never change mechanics, under the rule against a visible morality meter.
Under PRESS, WOLF holding back is presentation only. Tests must prove that the controls, the drop recovery and the engineer-only route are identical under both choices.

Byte-comparing tests (impact_test, junction_test, sentry_test) and every knockdown-restore assertion change meaning. Deaths no longer restore autosave A or B, so the tests must be rewritten deliberately, not loosened.
This changes the inventory design's rule that pickups patch beat_snapshot only: pickups must write to disk. Coordinate this with the v5 inventory work to avoid two migrations.
Placing the junction station at about x 500 may clash with CHOICE_X ≈ 526, WOLF_RUBBLE_X 448 or the blown-door art. A geometry test decides, with a fallback of about x 140.

Nothing here was played. Every timing is worked out from constants (190 px/s walk, 6 s build, 3 s cloud). The feel, the pacing and the 25 s worst case must be checked hands-on in a normal window with a separate save before any claim.

Scope mismatch: the relayed user request was to update the hero and main-screen background art everywhere with Codex. This death and safe-point design does not address it, and that request still needs its own step.
test_plan: Headless tests only; none of these show game feel. Run them with Godot 4.7.2 headless and an isolated test save path.
m0_state_test, v5 round trip: to_dict and from_dict keep safe_point, the case lists, dropped and falls_witnessed. Lists are written sorted, and two identical states produce identical bytes.

m0_state_test, v5 rejections:
- unknown safe_point
- safe_point room later than chapter_id
- junction safe_point without door_blown
- overlapping or duplicate or unknown ids
- the tool id in lost
- a derived REC id in any list
- dropped.x outside 40-920
- dropped x+14 > 452 in the junction while the door is unblown
- falls_witnessed outside 0..2
- junction flags with chapter_id before junction

m0_state_test, v4 to v5 migration: lockdown and corridor go to corridor, Records goes to records, junction with door sealed goes to records, junction with door blown goes to junction. All existing entries become secured, falls_witnessed is 0, and the relay memory is byte-identical.

junction_test, blast death: standing at x 400 when the fuse ends calls _die('blast'), not _fail_beat. door_blown stays true. The respawn is the last station used. Memory, route and the Records flags are unchanged. The disk was written before the card became active.

sentry_test, sentry death: contact during a chase kills. After respawn, sentry_down is still false, the sentry patrols from 840, lane_choice is kept for the session and the lane question is not re-asked.
junction_test, coolant: 1.1 s in a row inside the cloud does not kill and staying does. Leaving and re-entering resets the timer. The stagger never releases or blocks the movement actions.
impact_test, vent knockdown: _fail_beat still restores beat_snapshot. The case is unchanged, safe_point is unchanged and nothing is written.

Case drop: pick up [OBJECT_JUNCTION] (written as unsecured), die in the lane. The item is in dropped with room=junction and the death x. One USE at the drop recovers it as unsecured. In a second run, die again without recovering: the item is in lost. A tool dropped twice returns to its pickup x and is never lost.

Securing at a station: a held USE at each of the three stations moves every unsecured id to secured, sets safe_point and its positions, and writes. A hold released early changes nothing. The junction station refuses before door_blown.

Respawn: with only the corridor station used, a junction death resumes in the corridor at 876. The Records and junction rooms are still solved (traces, chapter_complete, door_blown). Re-entry shows the condensed lines, with no wolf_scouting and no authored entry text. The same scenario using the Records station resumes at about x 690.

Quit and Continue: after a pickup, quitting to title then Continue resumes at the last station with the item still unsecured. After a death, quitting during the card then Continue has the drop already applied. Continue with no save stays disabled and shows NO_CHECKPOINT_NOTE.

WOLF reactions: the death reaction branch and the respawn line tier depend only on memory.choice_id and falls_witnessed, the latter capped at 2. Under PRESS the engineer's controls, the drop recovery and the engineer-only route complete identically to DISCLOSE.

A failed save write: force save_to_disk to fail during a death and during a station use. save_pending is set, the in-memory state is correct, the next USE retries and the error appears only in the system hint.

Geometry: the station reaches at x 876, about 690 and about 500 do not overlap any other interaction reach, hazard span, CHOICE_X, WOLF_RUBBLE_X or pickup spot. The junction station is outside the sentry's CHASE_MIN_X.
Reduced Motion: the death sequence skips the collapse tween and the shake, and keeps the drain, the tone, the caption and the card. The card never advances without USE.
Regression: the existing chapter_scene, m0_scene, hold_use, ui_controls and settings suites still pass. The byte fixtures are regenerated deliberately and the diff is reviewed.

Outside headless, still required before any feel claim: hands-on play of both relay routes through every death cause in a normal Godot window with a separate save, recording the actual repeat times against the 25 s budget.

scores.name: Secure the Evidence
scores.note: This is the safest base and the best fit. Deaths cost evidence, not replayed play. It keeps today's autosaves for quitting, so quitting stays free, and death commits to disk before the sequence starts. WOLF only witnesses, which fits the rules best. It has three weak spots. (1) Respawn still follows autosaves A and B, so the junction door SAFE POINT moves the retry by only a few pixels; it matters only for securing [OBJECT_JUNCTION]. (2) Items return to their original spot, so there is no walk back to a drop, and a Records find is simply gone. That loss is permanent, not recoverable. (3) Its door station reach (452-490) overlaps the valve reach (VALVE_X 420 ±52 = 368-472). main.gd:1304 still answers USE there after door_blown ('The valve is spent'), so the station must move to 474 or further right. I checked against the code that the restore paths it reuses exist and match the description: _fail_beat (main.gd:1706), _restore_beat (1740), _write_beat (1249) and the dead branch at 1163.

scores.name: Two Falls, One Rest
scores.note: Safe points matter most here, because a second fall sends you back to the last rest. The cost of that is too high. The WOLF pull lets relay honesty change survival odds, which goes against the rule that choices carry no automatic penalty (the draft admits this). Removing the Records and junction autosaves in favour of a one-shot suspend file adds a second save format and an unusual v4 migration, and a crash can lose about 90 s. Skipping the optional rubble rest makes a second lane fall replay the solved door puzzle, which AbleGamers advises against. The SHAKEN tier is one more hidden rule players would have to learn. The good parts to borrow are the 2.4 s and 0.8 s card minimums and the rubble station at about x 496 with reach ±22 (474-518), which clears the valve reach and CHOICE_X 526.

scores.name: Secure Copy
scores.note: This draft has the strongest ideas: unsecured finds drop at the spot where you died and can be recovered once (Hollow Knight, Shovel Knight), and WOLF's capped respawn lines show that he remembers watching you die, with no change to mechanics. The cross-room respawn is the expensive part. You could wake in the corridor after a junction death. That separates the resume room from chapter_id, loosens the v4 rule that keeps junction flags false outside the junction, and needs solved rooms to support re-entry with condensed lines. That is a lot of new state for an 8 s walk through rooms the player has already solved. Keeping the door blown after a blast death lets players 'solve' the blast by dying. Writing every pickup to disk also changes the approved inventory rule. Borrow the drop and the WOLF lines, and leave out the cross-room respawn.

recommended.name: Secure the Evidence, with a recoverable drop (Draft 1 base, plus Draft 3's dropped case and WOLF memory lines, plus Draft 2's station placement and card timing)
recommended.pitch: Death is real, and the retry is close by. What dying costs is evidence the engineer has not yet protected. Lethal hazards kill: the door blast, the sentry catching you during a chase, and staying in the coolant cloud. Vent steam stays a knockdown with no cost, as it is today. After a death you retry at the last restore point in this room, which is the junction's entry autosave or a junction SAFE POINT you used later. Anything picked up since your last SAFE POINT falls as one 'dropped case' at the spot where you died. One tap recovers it. If you die again before you recover it, the entries become LOST for this save, and the case says so honestly, naming the room. A SAFE POINT is a quiet held-USE ritual in a hazard-free spot. Using one backs up the case so nothing in it can drop, makes that station your retry point in the room, saves the game, and gives WOLF a moment he chooses for himself. Facts are never lost: solved puzzles, story flags, the relay memory and its exact words, and the derived Records traces. Quitting never costs anything. There is no accessibility toggle, because repeats are capped at about 30 s and the stake is optional evidence, never progress. WOLF witnesses, and never rescues. Everything here is a proposal; none of it has been built or played.
recommended.on_death:
Lethal hazards, all in the Service Junction:
- Door blast: standing in 360-540 when the fuse ends.
- Sentry contact, only while it is chasing.
- Coolant cloud: dwelling inside it longer than CLOUD_LETHAL_SECONDS, about 1.0-1.2 s, with a choke and frost build-up as the warning. Crossing takes about 0.7 s at 190 px/s, so walking through is safe; to be tuned in play.
Vent steam keeps the _fail_beat knockdown exactly as it works today.

Death (a new _die_beat(cause), separate from _fail_beat):
1. COMMIT on the first frame, before any animation:
   - Choose the restore point: the latest disk write (autosave A, B, or the junction SAFE POINT if used), or beat_snapshot when save_pending is set.
   - Any existing `dropped` set becomes `lost`.
   - Every unsecured entry moves to `dropped`, with x set to the death x. Clamp it to walkable floor, and while the door is unblown keep x+14 ≤ 452.
   - Write to disk. A write failure uses today's save_pending and SAVE_FAILED_HINT, and the loss still applies in memory.
2. SEQUENCE: grim, not gory.
   - Gameplay actions are released.
   - Collapse. With Reduced Motion this is a cut to the fallen pose.
   - All sound ducks to one ringing tone, volume-capped and captioned.
   - The screen drains to grey and then dark, with no flashing.
   - WOLF reacts by his own choice: with DISCLOSE he rushes in and stays; with PRESS he holds at a distance and looks away.
   - The first death in a beat takes about 4-5 s; a repeat death in the same beat takes about 2 s.
3. DEATH CARD:
   - One line naming the cause.
   - If anything dropped, a 'case dropped' line and the case-with-a-gap icon, so it reads as text and shape.
   - Accepts USE after 2.4 s on the first death of a beat and 0.8 s on a repeat. Never auto-advances. Pause and Back work.
4. RETRY:
   - Fade in at the restore point. A blast death returns to autosave A, so the door is still sealed and the puzzle is redone; no solving it by dying.
   - Sentry and cloud deaths return to the later of autosave B and the junction SAFE POINT.
   - The dropped case glints where you fell.
   - The pressure line, sentry, arm and cloud re-sync as _sync_junction_room does today.
   - lane_choice persists for the session, so WOLF does not re-ask the lane question.
   - WOLF's first line after respawn is chosen from choice_id and a session-only witnessed count capped at 2. From the third death on he gives a look only.
recommended.what_safe_points_do:
A SAFE POINT is a lit station. Hold USE for about 1.0-1.2 s, reusing hold_use; the touch label reads SECURE and letting go cancels. Completing the hold does five things:
1. SECURE: secured = collected. A dropped case that has already been recovered is secured too. A short status line and a lock chirp confirm it, with no counts.
2. RETRY POINT: _save_progress() at the station sets safe_point_id. Later deaths in this room retry here.
3. SAVE: the normal atomic write.
4. REST: room tone ducks, a short procedural safe-room motif plays, and the station is out of reach of every hazard.
5. WOLF MOMENT, chosen by WOLF, with no mechanical effect: with DISCLOSE he settles beside the engineer; with PRESS he keeps watch from the room edge. At most one authored line per station, conditioned on real state.

The corridor station teaches securing on first use. Unlimited uses. With nothing to secure, a use still saves and rests. Fix the dead branch at main.gd:1163 so a repeat corridor use secures, rests and saves before the second USE enters Records.
recommended.what_is_lost_and_kept:
LOST on death:
- Position, back to the restore point. At most about 30 s of play.
- Live hazard progress.
- UNSECURED evidence: it becomes DROPPED at the death spot and can be recovered once with a tap.
- A previous unrecovered drop becomes LOST for this save. It is shown in the case with its room, never hidden.
- Examined and annotated marks travel with their entries.

KEPT always:
- Every story and world flag.
- The relay memory, byte for byte.
- The derived purge and mirror traces, which are never at risk.
- Secured entries.
- lane_choice, for the session.
- The carried tool: if it is ever lost, it returns to its pickup spot instead of becoming LOST.

KNOCKDOWN (vent): nothing is lost.

What can actually be at stake in this slice, by design: [OBJECT_JUNCTION], held before the junction SAFE POINT, and [DATA_RECORDS] if the Records SAFE POINT was skipped. That is two optional entries at most. Nothing required is ever at risk, and the game still finishes with an empty case.

Never shown: no death counter, no percentage, no score.
recommended.wolf_role:
WOLF is an independent witness, and survival never depends on him.
- Death reaction, chosen from the relay memory: rush in (DISCLOSE) or hold back (PRESS). Presentation only.
- Respawn lines: a capped tier keyed to choice_id and a witnessed count of 0, 1 or 2+, kept as session memory and never shown. From the third death on, a look only, so the lines do not repeat into comedy.
- Safe-point moment: settle close or keep watch.

judged.recommendation_plain: Go with 'Secure the Evidence' and add two ideas from the other drafts. Dying is real: the engineer collapses, the sound fades to a ringing tone, WOLF reacts, and you try again nearby, so you never replay more than about half a minute. What dying costs is evidence. Anything you picked up since your last safe point drops where you died. You can walk back and grab it once, but if you die again first, it's lost. Safe points are quiet places where you rest, WOLF settles with you, and your evidence is locked in for good. Solved puzzles, your choices and what WOLF remembers are never undone, and quitting never costs anything. Vent steam still only knocks you down. WOLF never rescues you, so being honest with him never changes your odds of surviving. Nothing here has been built or played yet.
questions_for_user: If you die twice before picking your dropped evidence back up, should it be lost for good, or quietly go back to where you first found it?
If the door blast kills you, should the door be sealed again so you redo that short puzzle (my recommendation), or stay blown open?
Should WOLF's reaction to a death stay wordless, or should he say something? And are you happy that he never rescues the engineer?

Your actual request was to update the hero image and the game's main-screen background everywhere using Codex, and this step didn't touch that. Should that be the next task, and which images and places should change?
